title: Candidate-mechanism plausibility can outrun denominator-scale association evidence
summary: A candidate pattern linking candidate-gene failures and denominator-scale calibration, now explicitly bounded by positive controls and denominator-diversity caveats. Rev0020 adds HLA-B*15:02/carbamazepine and PCSK9 controls and points the pattern toward phenotype tightness, effect size, actionability, diversity, and portability rather than anti-genetics.

status_history.note: Created after three psychiatric/behavioral genetics records and two infrastructure records; no maturity upgrade.
Added APOE, HLA-B*5701/abacavir, and ADH1B/ALDH2 positive-control records plus curation infrastructure; pattern remains candidate-only.
Added HLA-B*15:02/carbamazepine and PCSK9 controls plus MKH-PAT-0016 denominator-diversity scope pattern.

time.evidence_window: pre-GWAS candidate-gene era through GWAS/consortium-era correction records

subjects.name: candidate mechanism plausibility vs denominator-scale calibration

claims.claim: The depression candidate-gene, 5-HTTLPR×stress, and schizophrenia candidate-gene records support a candidate pattern: plausible biological targets can generate large literatures and memorable claims before denominator-scale testing, power, and multiple-comparison standards are strong enough to calibrate them.
what_would_change_status: A positive-control and negative-control pass shows this family is too broad, too narrow, or should be split into power, theory-selection, and data-infrastructure subpatterns.

claims.claim: The GWAS Catalog and PGC records support the correction-rail side of the pattern: genome-wide, consortium-scale, summary-statistics-enabled infrastructures changed which associations could be tested and reused, while still preserving statistical-association, data-sharing, diversity, and ethics limits.
what_would_change_status: Future evidence shows these infrastructures do not function as denominator/correction rails for this case family, or that the pattern should be represented only as a method note.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0015 remains candidate-only and explicitly excludes anti-hypothesis, anti-genetics, or “candidate genes always fail” overclaims; maturation requires positive controls such as well-established candidate-gene successes, negative controls, and ancestry/phenotype caveats.
what_would_change_status: At least one positive-control, one negative-control, and one split/merge decision make the pattern mature or lead to rollback.

claims.claim: Rev0019 positive controls show that MKH-PAT-0015 must be read as a calibration pattern, not an anti-candidate-gene rule: APOE, HLA-B*5701/abacavir, and ADH1B/ALDH2 preserve cases where genetic evidence remains useful under tighter phenotype, mechanism, population, or actionability conditions.
what_would_change_status: A red-team pass finds these are not valid controls for the historical candidate-gene pattern because their evidence routes or phenotype classes are too different.

claims.claim: The pattern remains candidate-only after the controls: the new evidence implies the pattern should be split or conditioned around phenotype tightness, mechanism/effect size, denominator breadth, population scope, and actionability; no frequency or causal theory claims are allowed.
what_would_change_status: A future synthesis satisfies the maturity gate with controls, caveat records, split/merge decisions, and second-pass source review.

evidence_refs.support_type: candidate status, red-team controls, and maturity gate

claims.claim: Rev0020 strengthens MKH-PAT-0015 by adding two further positive controls: HLA-B*15:02/carbamazepine shows actionable but ancestry-scoped pharmacogenomics, while PCSK9 loss-of-function shows a strong-effect human-genetic relation; together they push the pattern toward axes such as phenotype tightness, effect size, actionability, and evidence scope.
what_would_change_status: If second-pass review shows these controls are not comparable to the candidate-gene family, split them into separate pattern-control families.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0016 now qualifies MKH-PAT-0015: candidate-gene denominator failure cannot be interpreted without population diversity, portability, trait architecture, governance, and data-source coverage; no maturity upgrade is allowed until this scope layer is reviewed.
what_would_change_status: If the denominator-diversity pattern is merged into a broader external-validity pattern, update this qualification edge.

evidence_refs.support_type: denominator diversity and portability scope pattern

evidence_profile.source_basis: two NEG records, one MET record, three CTL positive-control records, three INF records, plus direct source records; all one-pass
limitations: Positive controls are now present but only one-pass reviewed.
No negative-control or counterexample record has been promoted yet.
No ancestry/diversity and phenotype-quality caveat record has been promoted yet.
No mature split/merge decision has separated power failure, theory-selection failure, phenotype mismatch, and denominator-infrastructure effects.

type_payload.short_definition: When early evidence selects targets by biological plausibility and small samples, durable claims can form before the field can see the denominator of tested/untested alternatives; later high-throughput, consortium-scale, multiple-testing-aware evidence can shrink, overturn, or redirect those claims.

case_evidence.mechanism: large-sample nonconfirmation of depression candidate gene main-effect and G×E hypotheses
collaborative meta-analysis nonconfirmation of famous 5-HTTLPR×stress interaction
historical schizophrenia candidate-gene literature audited against GWAS-era denominator evidence
GWAS Catalog exposes genome-wide association and summary-statistics surfaces
PGC provides consortium-scale psychiatric genomics analysis/data rail
positive control: APOE ε4 risk relation with explicit non-determinism
positive control: ADH1B/ALDH2 biochemical pathway and population-scoped GWAS signal
curation/actionability rail distinguishing association, validity, and implementation

not_this: not a claim that genetic association research is futile
not a claim that all candidate-gene hypotheses fail
not a claim that GWAS proves causation
not a stigma surface for psychiatric illness
needed_before_synthesis: Promote at least one negative-control/counterexample record where candidate plausibility is present but denominator-scale evidence supports rather than overturns the hypothesis under comparable common-trait conditions.
Add ancestry/diversity and phenotype-quality caveat records.
Perform a split/merge decision: power failure vs theory-selection failure vs phenotype mismatch vs infrastructure denominator expansion vs actionability.
Second-pass source review of all positive controls and failed-candidate records.

positive_controls_needed: First positive-control pass is present, but second-pass review must decide whether APOE, HLA-B*5701/abacavir, and ADH1B/ALDH2 are comparable controls or belong in distinct subfamilies.
negative_controls_needed: Add at least one negative/control contrast where candidate plausibility and a tight phenotype did not survive denominator-scale testing.
Add at least one case where a narrow-denominator genetic finding transferred robustly across populations after careful testing.
Add at least one therapy-target genetic positive that later failed clinical translation, if source-acquired.
counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where small, mechanistically chosen candidate variants were robust before high-throughput genomics under comparable common-trait conditions.
Cases where GWAS denominator expansion missed a biologically central locus later found by another method.
Cases where a strong pharmacogenomic or enzyme-pathway relation misled practice due to poor actionability or population transfer.
Cases where denominator diversity was limited but the association or clinical actionability was robust across later external validation.
Cases where diversity expansion alone did not repair portability because measurement or environment dominated.
rollback_triggers: The pattern becomes indistinguishable from generic low-power/publication-bias patterns and should be merged into MKH-PAT-0009 or a broader denominator pattern.
Positive controls show that the real axis is phenotype tightness/effect size/actionability, not candidate plausibility vs denominator scale.
Ancestry/phenotype caveats dominate enough that the pattern must split into subpatterns.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: Positive controls, negative controls, ancestry/phenotype caveat records, a split/merge memo, and second-pass source review of every direct supporting claim.

handling_notes: Psychiatric genetics is a stigmatization-sensitive domain; never imply biological determinism, group inferiority, or clinical prediction beyond sources.
Early researchers should be treated historically and methodologically, not as ridicule targets.
Population diversity, consent, privacy, and phenotype quality are part of the pattern’s validity, not footnotes.

unknowns: Whether APOE, HLA-B*5701/abacavir, and ADH1B/ALDH2 are comparable controls for psychiatric candidate-gene literatures or belong in a separate “tight phenotype / large effect / actionability” family.
Whether MKH-PAT-0015 should split into power, phenotype, mechanism/effect-size, and infrastructure/actionability subpatterns.
How to encode ancestry/diversity and health-equity caveats without turning them into an afterthought.
next_actions: Promote a negative-control/counterexample record for MKH-PAT-0015.
Add ancestry/diversity and phenotype-quality caveat records for GWAS/psychiatric genomics.
Second-pass source APOE and HLA-B*5701 records from peer-reviewed review/guideline sources with page locators.
Write split/merge memo after one more control pass.
